processing: Fully oxidised black tea from Assam-type tea plants. The brand was built on organic and pesticide-free growing and on selecting plants from the seedling stage.
harvest_season: No fixed picking calendar is well recorded; makers state their own harvest.
appearance_dry: Typical of Assam-type black tea, dark twisted leaf with a reddish-brown cast.
appearance_liquor: Typically a clear, deep reddish brown.
taste_profile: Few tasting descriptions are on record; Assam-type black teas generally give a fuller, maltier cup than the gentler black teas of mainland Japan.

brewing.notes: A usual Western-style starting point for Assam-type tea. It should stand up to a splash of milk, but try it plain first.

vintage_note: Usual for its class, it is sold as a recent-harvest tea under the Ryukyu Koucha name and is best drunk within a year or two. It is not an ageing tea, and output is small compared with Japan's green tea.
description:
Ryukyu koucha is black tea from Okinawa, and the plant is what sets it apart. Okinawa's position suits Assam-type tea, the plant behind strong black teas, which is not what mainland Japan mostly grows.

It is as much a brand project as a tea. Growers set out to add value through organic and pesticide-free cultivation, selecting from the seedling stage, and the town of Kin became the centre of the local effort.

As with other Assam-type teas, expect more body and malt than from most Japanese black tea. Use hot water and a Western-style steep of about three minutes, then adjust.

Okinawa also has other local names, including Yamashiro and Yanbaru black tea, so check who made what you are buying.
history:
An attempt to grow Assam tea in Okinawa is recorded in 1958, but it did not take hold. Production began again in 2000 under the Ryukyu Koucha brand.

In 2008 the Kin town project to establish the tea as a local product received Japan Brand recognition and support as a regional resource from the national agency for small businesses, with sales abroad part of the plan.
